title: Fix some -Wmissing-variable-declarations errors.
description:
With Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.1.1.101) from Xcode 26.5, we
get some errors from -Wmissing-variable-declarations. Fix them:

Make some variables static if they're not used outside the file.

When generating plugin.c files for plugins, make them all include a new
wsutil/plugin_exports.h file, which declares the variables that plugins
export. Have that header also check whether WS_BUILD_DLL is set and fail
if it isn't; this checks whether plugins are being built correctly (it's
a requirement on Windows, at minimum).

This means that the plugin.c generator, tools/make-plugin-reg.py,
doesn't need to generate declarations of plugin_register(void) and
plugin_describe(void), as those are now done in the header in question.

Add the include of <wsutil/plugin_exports.h>, and remove the manual
declarations of the two functions, from
plugins/epan/dfilter/ipaddr/ipaddr.c - that plugin doesn't use a
generated plugin.c. (It probably should be changed to do so.)

Give a name to the parameter of addRemote(), so that we can properly
document it in the comment.

I observe one more which could be fixed.
```
/Users/stig/wireshark/epan/wslua/lrexlib/pcre2/lpcre2_f.c:100:11: warning: no previous extern declaration for non-static variable 'pcre2_error_flags' [-Wmissing-variable-declarations]
  100 | flag_pair pcre2_error_flags[] = {
      |           ^
```
This is a third party library. It's a very mature and stable one, but we might not want to patch it. Werror is not enabled in this directory. We could entirely suppress the warning.

> We could entirely suppress the warning.

Presumably meaning "don't enable -Wmissing-variable-declarations in this directory"?

(We might also want to suggest some of the staticizations upstream.)
Right, override the standard common flags with `-Wno-missing-variable-declarations` if the warning is set.

The plugin in `epan/dfilter/ipaddr.c` isn't processed by `make-plugin-reg.py`. It includes all the necessary functions already. It would need to manually include the header.

The directions in `doc` for out of the tree plugins perhaps should be updated to mention the new header.
Should this file check if `WS_BUILD_DLL` is defined already and either fail if not or define it? All the plugins define it first, but that might be a check for third party plugins.

> Should this file check if `WS_BUILD_DLL` is defined already and either fail if not or define it? ...
> ...that might be a check for third party plugins.

Yes, it should; that would be a good error check.
Done. (I commented out the definition of `WS_BUILD_DLL` in one of the generated plugin.c file and built; it failed as expected.)

Doing this broke the Debian and Ubuntu package builds, because there's some part in the `packaging/debian/rules` file that checks that all the headers can be compiled. I guess this would have to be special cased. I'm not that familiar with Debian packages, so someone like @rbalint helping would be nice.

https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/jobs/14428860621

> Doing this broke the Debian and Ubuntu package builds, because there's some part in the `packaging/debian/rules` file that checks that all the headers can be compiled. I guess this would have to be special cased.

Or, once we fix plugins/epan/dfilter/ipaddr to generate a plugins.c file, get rid of the header and put the declarations into plugins.c, assuming compilers don't treat that as cheating.
We could, although I do like the idea of having a header that third party plugin authors could include to remind them which symbols need to be defined.
Looks like GCC requires this to be `WS_DLL_PUBLIC_DEF` (avoiding the `extern`) if declared in a header now.

> Looks like GCC requires this to be `WS_DLL_PUBLIC_DEF` (avoiding the `extern`) if declared in a header now.

Umm, why? Those are all declarations, as in "this is defined Somewhere Else", not definitions, as in "this is the place where it's defined".

Strike that, just eliminate these two lines to avoid a "redundant declaration" warning/error now that the two are declared in the header. `WS_DLL_PUBLIC_DEF` presumably isn't needed for the definition so long as the right symbol is on the declaration.

To quote include/ws_symbol_export.h:

```
#if defined _WIN32 || defined __CYGWIN__
  /* Compiling for Windows, so we use the Windows DLL declarations. */
  #ifdef WS_BUILD_DLL
    /*
     * Building a DLL; for all definitions, we want dllexport, and
     * (presumably so source from DLL and source from a program using the
     * DLL can both include a header that declares APIs and exported data
     * for the DLL), for declarations, either dllexport or dllimport will
     * work (they mean the same thing for a declaration when building a DLL).
     */
    #ifdef __GNUC__
      /* GCC */
      #define WS_DLL_PUBLIC_DEF __attribute__ ((dllexport))
    #else /* ! __GNUC__ */
      /*
       * Presumably MSVC.
       * Note: actually gcc seems to also support this syntax.
       */
      #define WS_DLL_PUBLIC_DEF __declspec(dllexport)
    #endif /* __GNUC__ */
```

so the difference between `WS_DLL_PUBLIC` and `WS_DLL_PUBLIC_DEF` is a Windows requirement, as Windows draws a distinction between "this is a declaration that imports a symbol from a DLL" and "this is a declaration of or a definition of a symbol that's defined in this DLL".

"These two" presumably refers to the function declarations. The redundant ones are the ones being done in plugin.c, so we should probably change tools/make-plugin-reg.py not to generate those declarations.
Done.

> The plugin in `epan/dfilter/ipaddr.c` isn't processed by `make-plugin-reg.py`.

Should it be?

Maybe. I think that one was initially developed as an out of the tree plugin and then added without adding all the magic in `make-plugin-reg.py` for the new class of dfilter plugins. However, if added, we might have to remove the now redundant declaration of functions that the registration script adds to the local `plugin.c`.

> However, if added, we might have to remove the now redundant declaration of functions that the registration script adds to the local `plugin.c`.

I manually added an include of <wsutil/plugin_exports.h> and removed the declarations of those functions. I'll look at having a generated plugin.c in a separate commit.
